walkthroughs.body_html:
Chemical Bonding HL — a core area of Chemistry.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Chemical Bonding HL brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Chemical Bonding HL.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Lewis dot structures were proposed in:
What does an NMR chemical shift (δ, in ppm) actually measure?
options: Water is bent because oxygen is heavier than hydrogen and weighs the middle down.
The position of a peak RELATIVE to TMS (tetramethylsilane, δ = 0), normalised by the spectrometer frequency.
Chemical shift is the mass of the molecule divided by 1000.
Chemical shift is the absolute resonance frequency of the nucleus in Hz.

mcqs.q: At which electrode are positive ions reduced during electrolysis?
options: Water is bent because oxygen is heavier than hydrogen and weighs the middle down.
At the cathode (the negative electrode) — positive ions gain electrons there.
Positive ions are oxidised at the cathode by losing protons.
Positive ions are reduced at the anode because that's where positive things go.

mcqs.q: Why does water have a bent shape rather than linear?
options: Water is bent because the hydrogens repel each other and push apart.
Water is bent because oxygen is heavier than hydrogen and weighs the middle down.
Oxygen has two bonding pairs and two lone pairs, giving a tetrahedral electron geometry but a bent molecular shape.
Positive ions are oxidised at the cathode by losing protons.
